verdict.rationale: Trello's own REST API docs describe generating an API key and issuing user tokens through a delegated authorization flow (the `1/authorize` route or OAuth1.0), where token lifetime and permission scope are configurable via query params. That covers issuing scoped, expiring credentials an agent could use. The evidence is a single thin line on scoping, so how fine-grained the least privilege can be (e.g., per-board or per-action limits) is not shown. Missing for 10: documented scope granularity (which scopes exist and whether access can be limited per board or workspace), any agent- or service-account-specific credential type, documented revocation or audit of issued tokens, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
